$comment: (atlas-autonomy) THE READER'S OWN CASES. Questions the reader met while using Atlas, each with the outcome they would have wanted, in their own words. Appended with `node scripts/atlas-eval/add-case.mjs --text "…" --ideal "…"`; nothing else writes this file.

They are asked like the open questions (scripts/atlas-eval/open-questions.json — an ordinary question, no instruction about HOW to show the answer) and graded on the same axes. `ideal` is a REFERENCE handed to the independent grader beside the reply — what a reader who knows the subject would have wanted to come away with — and never a key: the verdict does not turn on matching it, and no machine check reads it. Anything a machine CAN decide (the same object, a colour, a count, a control that changes what is shown) belongs in questions.json's mapState/deliverables, where it is checked against the real map, not here.
Write `ideal` as the outcome, not the method: what the reader should understand or be able to do afterwards. A method written here would be a thing to memorise.
